I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for over forty years. I know the soil here, I know the water table, I know what the neighbors grow. At my age, with my back the way it is, I'm not going to experiment. I plant what this land is for: winter wheat and summer maize. That's the rotation I've done my whole life and my father did before me.

My land is about 8 mu. Not much, but it's mine. My son is in Shijiazhuang working in construction, so I manage alone mostly, with help from my wife during harvest.

For wheat, I'll plant in October like always. The county extension office gave us improved Jimai seeds a few years back and the yield was noticeably better, so I kept buying that type. I'll rotary-till before planting — my tractor neighbor helps me with that. I irrigate three times: once before overwintering, once at jointing, once at heading. The groundwater pump we share in the village handles that. I'll put down base fertilizer when I plant, then topdress in spring. Two rounds of pesticide — one for rust, one for aphids before heading.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant corn on the same ground without plowing — just direct seeding into the stubble. Corn is easier. Hybrid seed, same field, one or two waterings depending on the rain. Harvest in September, then prepare again for wheat.

I won't grow vegetables beyond what we eat ourselves. Cotton is too much trouble now with my hands.
